principle_text: When the persuadee shares information about their volunteer experience, avoid only stating your own involvement without connecting it to the donation goal or eliciting their donation intent.
When the persuadee shares information about their volunteering experience, avoid asking questions that do not directly connect to the donation goal or the specific charity you want to promote.

When the persuadee shows hesitation or uncertainty about the effectiveness of a charity, avoid providing only general support statements without addressing their concerns or offering evidence of impact.
When the persuadee expresses concerns about misuse and waste in nonprofits, avoid ignoring these concerns and instead acknowledge and address them directly to build trust.

When the persuadee acknowledges the importance of basic needs but does not respond directly to cost-effectiveness information, avoid relying solely on statistics without connecting them to the persuadee's values or concerns.
